page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine from the Dpldsv6 series, powered by Microsoft's custom ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture. The instance provisions 48 dedicated physical cores running at 3.4 GHz with one thread per core, accompanied by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache. It supplies 96.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, and includes 2,835 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Acceleration hardware is not included, as there are zero GPUs present.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput. The server achieved a top-tier multi-core Geekbench score of 22,029 and a strong stress-ng multi-core result of 99,380.68, contrasting with mid-tier single-core execution metrics. Memory performance is a distinct strength, reaching top-tier bandwidths of 464.03 GB/sec for uncached reads and 200.4 GB/sec for writes, which fuels high database and cache transaction rates, such as 89.96 million Redis SET operations per second and top-tier PassMark database scores. Static web serving throughput reaches 74.8 GB/sec.

Operating on an ARM instruction set with a 1:2 memory-to-core allocation, the D48plds_v6 provides high compute density and localized disk throughput without the overhead of excess RAM. It is particularly effective for continuous integration and multi-threaded compilation, clustered caching layers, distributed databases needing low-latency NVMe scratch space, and web serving fleets that benefit from high core counts and fast I/O.
description: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 architecture clocked at 3.4 GHz. Operating without hyperthreading, the instance allocates 96.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core alongside 2,835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark evaluation reveals top-tier multi-threaded compute performance and memory bandwidth, reaching 464.03 GB/sec on large-block reads and delivering strong throughput in Clang software compilation and Redis operations. Because single-core scores fall within the middle tier and RAM capacity is reduced compared to standard general-purpose tiers, the configuration prioritizes raw parallel core throughput and rapid local disk access over single-threaded burst capability. It is well aligned with parallel build pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, and database workloads requiring high local I/O performance.
